title: Voting: justifications
description: Explaining a voting outcome by axioms: the abstraction guesses axiom instances and profiles, the check looks for outcomes that satisfy them but differ from the target outcome. Each instance is one question: a set of axioms, a target profile and its outcome (Instances tab).

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
%%% The voting/justification setting
candidate(1..num_candidates).
position(1..num_candidates).

voter(1..num_voters).

profile_num(1..num_profiles).


% Auxiliary
swap(C1,C2,C1,C2) :-
    candidate(C1), candidate(C2), C1 < C2.
swap(C1,C2,C2,C1) :-
    candidate(C1), candidate(C2), C1 < C2.
swap(C1,C2,C3,C3) :-
    candidate(C1), candidate(C2), C1 < C2,
    candidate(C3), C3 != C1, C3 != C2.

%%% The axioms. An instance switches axioms on with facts use_axiom(A), for A in
%%% pareto, faithfulness, unanimity, cancellation, reinforcement, condorcet,
%%% neutrality2, pos_responsiveness. It also gives the target profile
%%% target_profile(Voter,Candidate,Position) (in lexicographic order), the target
%%% outcome target_outcome(C), optionally requires_polarity_axiom, and the constants
%%% num_candidates, num_voters, num_profiles and num_axiom_instances.

axiom(pareto(C)) :- candidate(C),
    use_axiom(pareto).
pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),pareto(C)) :-
    use_axiom(pareto),
    profile_num(Prof), axiom(pareto(C)).

axiom(faithfulness) :-
    use_axiom(faithfulness).
pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),faithfulness) :-
    use_axiom(faithfulness),
    profile_num(Prof), axiom(faithfulness).

axiom(unanimity) :-
    use_axiom(unanimity).
pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),unanimity) :-
    use_axiom(unanimity),
    profile_num(Prof), axiom(unanimity).

axiom(cancellation) :-
    use_axiom(cancellation).
pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),cancellation) :-
    use_axiom(cancellation),
    profile_num(Prof), axiom(cancellation).

axiom(reinforcement) :-
    use_axiom(reinforcement).
reinforcement_triple(Prof1,Prof2,Prof3) :-
    use_axiom(reinforcement),
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2), Prof1 <= Prof2,
    profile_num(Prof3),
    Prof1 < Prof3, Prof2 < Prof3. % only allowed due to symmetry breaking
reinforcement_triple(Prof1,Prof2,1) :-
    use_axiom(reinforcement),
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2), Prof1 <= Prof2.
pos_axiom_instance(triple(Prof1,Prof2,Prof3),reinforcement) :-
    use_axiom(reinforcement),
    reinforcement_triple(Prof1,Prof2,Prof3),
    axiom(reinforcement).

axiom(condorcet(C)) :- candidate(C),
    use_axiom(condorcet).
pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),condorcet(C)) :-
    use_axiom(condorcet),
    profile_num(Prof), axiom(condorcet(C)).

axiom(neutrality2(C1,C2)) :- candidate(C1), candidate(C2), C1 < C2,
    use_axiom(neutrality2).
pos_axiom_instance(double(Prof1,Prof2),neutrality2(C1,C2)) :-
    use_axiom(neutrality2),
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2), Prof1 <= Prof2,
    axiom(neutrality2(C1,C2)).

pos_response_pair(C,P) :-
    use_axiom(pos_responsiveness),
    candidate(C), position(P), P < num_candidates.
axiom(pos_responsiveness(V,C,P)) :-
    use_axiom(pos_responsiveness),
    voter(V), pos_response_pair(C,P).
pos_axiom_instance(double(Prof1,Prof2),pos_responsiveness(V,C,P)) :-
    use_axiom(pos_responsiveness),
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2),
    axiom(pos_responsiveness(V,C,P)).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
%%% Guess profiles
{ active_voter(Prof,V) } :- profile_num(Prof), voter(V).
:- active_voter(Prof,V), not active_voter(Prof,V-1), voter(V), voter(V-1).
active_profile(Prof) :- profile_num(Prof), active_voter(Prof,1).
:- active_profile(Prof), profile_num(Prof-1), not active_profile(Prof-1).

1 { profile(Prof,V,Cand,Pos) : position(Pos) } 1 :-
    profile_num(Prof), voter(V), active_voter(Prof,V), candidate(Cand).
1 { profile(Prof,V,Cand,Pos) : candidate(Cand) } 1 :-
    profile_num(Prof), voter(V), active_voter(Prof,V), position(Pos).

%%% Symmetry breaking: lexicographical ordering within each profile
lex_eq_until(Prof,V1,V2,0) :-
    profile_num(Prof), voter(V1), voter(V2), V1 < V2.
lex_eq_until(Prof,V1,V2,Pos) :-
    profile_num(Prof), voter(V1), voter(V2), V1 < V2,
    position(Pos), lex_eq_until(Prof,V1,V2,Pos-1),
    profile(Prof,V1,C,Pos), profile(Prof,V2,C,Pos).
lex_dom(Prof,V1,V2) :- profile_num(Prof), voter(V1), voter(V2), V1 < V2,
    profile(Prof,V1,C1,Pos), profile(Prof,V2,C2,Pos), C2 < C1,
    lex_eq_until(Prof,V1,V2,Pos-1).
:- profile_num(Prof), lex_dom(Prof,V1,V2), voter(V1), voter(V2), V1 < V2,
    active_voter(Prof,V1), active_voter(Prof,V2).

%%% Make sure that the target profile appears with index 1
:- not profile(1,V,Cand,Pos), target_profile(V,Cand,Pos).
target_active_voter(V) :- target_profile(V,_,_).
:- active_voter(1,V), not target_active_voter(V).

%%% Shared for applicability of various axioms
num_active_voters(Prof,Num) :-
    profile_num(Prof), Num = #count { V : active_voter(Prof,V) }.
votes_identical(Prof1,V1,Prof2,V2) :-
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2),
    active_voter(Prof1,V1), active_voter(Prof2,V2),
    profile(Prof1,V1,C,P) : profile(Prof2,V2,C,P).
num_votes_identical(Prof1,V1,Prof2,N) :-
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2), voter(V1),
    N = #count { V2 : voter(V2), votes_identical(Prof1,V1,Prof2,V2) }.

%%% Applicability of PARETO
dominates_in_voter(Prof,V,C1,C2) :-
    use_axiom(pareto),
    profile_num(Prof), active_voter(Prof,V),
    candidate(C1), candidate(C2), C1 != C2,
    profile(Prof,V,C1,P1), profile(Prof,V,C2,P2), P1 < P2.
dominates_in_profile(Prof,C1,C2) :-
    use_axiom(pareto),
    profile_num(Prof),
    candidate(C1), candidate(C2), C1 != C2,
    dominates_in_voter(Prof,V,C1,C2) : active_voter(Prof,V).
axiom_applicable(single(Prof),pareto(C2)) :-
    use_axiom(pareto),
    pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),pareto(C2)),
    active_profile(Prof),
    dominates_in_profile(Prof,C1,C2), candidate(C1), C1 != C2.

%%% Applicability of FAITHFULNESS
axiom_applicable(single(Prof),faithfulness) :-
    use_axiom(faithfulness),
    pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),faithfulness),
    active_profile(Prof),
    active_voter(Prof,1), not active_voter(Prof,2).

%%% Applicability of UNANIMITY
axiom_applicable(single(Prof),unanimity) :-
    use_axiom(unanimity),
    pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),unanimity),
    active_profile(Prof), candidate(C),
    profile(Prof,V,C,1) : active_voter(Prof,V).

%%% Applicability of CANCELLATION
num_active_voters_even(Prof) :-
    use_axiom(cancellation),
    num_active_voters(Prof,Num), Num \ 2 == 0.
cancellation_flipped_pair(Prof,V1,V2) :-
    use_axiom(cancellation),
    num_active_voters_even(Prof), num_active_voters(Prof,Num),
    active_voter(Prof,V1), active_voter(Prof,V2), V1 < V2,
    V1 <= Num/2, V2 == Num-V1+1.
cancellation_identical_pair(Prof,V1,V2) :-
    use_axiom(cancellation),
    num_active_voters_even(Prof), num_active_voters(Prof,Num),
    active_voter(Prof,V1), active_voter(Prof,V2), V1 < V2,
    V1 <= Num/2, V2 <= Num/2.
cancellation_identical_pair(Prof,V1,V2) :-
    use_axiom(cancellation),
    num_active_voters_even(Prof), num_active_voters(Prof,Num),
    active_voter(Prof,V1), active_voter(Prof,V2), V1 < V2,
    V1 > Num/2, V2 > Num/2.
votes_identical(Prof,V1,V2) :-
    votes_identical(Prof,V1,Prof,V2), V1 < V2.
votes_flipped(Prof,V1,V2) :-
    use_axiom(cancellation),
    profile_num(Prof), active_voter(Prof,V1), active_voter(Prof,V2), V1 < V2,
    profile(Prof,V2,C,num_candidates-P+1) : profile(Prof,V1,C,P).
axiom_applicable(single(Prof),cancellation) :-
    use_axiom(cancellation),
    pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),cancellation),
    active_profile(Prof),
    num_active_voters_even(Prof),
    votes_identical(Prof,V1,V2) : cancellation_identical_pair(Prof,V1,V2);
    votes_flipped(Prof,V1,V2) : cancellation_flipped_pair(Prof,V1,V2).

%%% Applicability of REINFORCEMENT
reinforcement_count_check(triple(Prof1,Prof2,Prof3),V) :-
    use_axiom(reinforcement),
    pos_axiom_instance(triple(Prof1,Prof2,Prof3),reinforcement),
    active_voter(Prof3,V),
    num_votes_identical(Prof3,V,Prof1,N1),
    num_votes_identical(Prof3,V,Prof2,N2),
    num_votes_identical(Prof3,V,Prof3,N3),
    N3 = N1 + N2.
axiom_applicable(triple(Prof1,Prof2,Prof3),reinforcement) :-
    use_axiom(reinforcement),
    pos_axiom_instance(triple(Prof1,Prof2,Prof3),reinforcement),
    active_profile(Prof1), active_profile(Prof2), active_profile(Prof3),
    num_active_voters(Prof1,N1), num_active_voters(Prof2,N2),
    num_active_voters(Prof3,N3), N3 = N1 + N2,
    reinforcement_count_check(triple(Prof1,Prof2,Prof3),V) :
        active_voter(Prof3,V).

%%% Applicability of CONDORCET
beats(Prof,V,C1,C2) :-
    use_axiom(condorcet),
    profile_num(Prof), active_voter(Prof,V),
    candidate(C1), candidate(C2), C1 != C2,
    profile(Prof,V,C1,P1), profile(Prof,V,C2,P2), P1 < P2.
majority_beats(Prof,C1,C2) :-
    use_axiom(condorcet),
    profile_num(Prof), candidate(C1), candidate(C2), C1 != C2,
    N1 = #count { V : beats(Prof,V,C1,C2) },
    N2 = #count { V : beats(Prof,V,C2,C1) },
    N1 > N2.
axiom_applicable(single(Prof),condorcet(C1)) :-
    use_axiom(condorcet),
    pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),condorcet(C1)),
    active_profile(Prof),
    majority_beats(Prof,C1,C2) : candidate(C2), C1 != C2.

%%% Applicability of NEUTRALITY/2
votes_identical_under_swap(Prof1,V1,Prof2,V2,C1,C2) :-
    use_axiom(neutrality2),
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2),
    active_voter(Prof1,V1), active_voter(Prof2,V2),
    candidate(C1), candidate(C2), C1 < C2,
    profile(Prof1,V1,CS2,P) : profile(Prof2,V2,CS1,P), swap(C1,C2,CS1,CS2).
num_votes_identical_under_swap(Prof1,V1,Prof2,C1,C2,N) :-
    use_axiom(neutrality2),
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2), voter(V1),
    candidate(C1), candidate(C2), C1 < C2,
    N = #count { V2 : voter(V2),
                      votes_identical_under_swap(Prof1,V1,Prof2,V2,C1,C2) }.
neutrality2_count_check(double(Prof1,Prof2),C1,C2,V) :-
    use_axiom(neutrality2),
    pos_axiom_instance(double(Prof1,Prof2),neutrality2(C1,C2)),
    active_voter(Prof1,V),
    num_votes_identical(Prof1,V,Prof1,N),
    num_votes_identical_under_swap(Prof1,V,Prof2,C1,C2,N).
axiom_applicable(double(Prof1,Prof2),neutrality2(C1,C2)) :-
    use_axiom(neutrality2),
    pos_axiom_instance(double(Prof1,Prof2),neutrality2(C1,C2)),
    active_profile(Prof1), active_profile(Prof2),
    num_active_voters(Prof1,N), num_active_voters(Prof2,N),
    neutrality2_count_check(double(Prof1,Prof2),C1,C2,V) :
        active_voter(Prof1,V).

%%% Applicability of POSITIVE RESPONSIVENESS
votes_identical_after_upwards_move(Prof1,V1,Prof2,V2,C,P) :-
    use_axiom(pos_responsiveness),
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2),
    active_voter(Prof1,V1), active_voter(Prof2,V2),
    pos_response_pair(C,P),
    profile(Prof1,V1,C,P1), profile(Prof2,V2,C,P1-P),
    profile(Prof2,V2,C2,P2) :
        profile(Prof1,V1,C2,P2), P2 > P1;
    profile(Prof2,V2,C2,P2) :
        profile(Prof1,V1,C2,P2), P2 < P1-P;
    profile(Prof2,V2,C2,P2+1) :
        profile(Prof1,V1,C2,P2), P2 < P1, P2 >= P1-P.
pos_response_check(Prof1,V1,Prof2,V2,C,P) :-
    use_axiom(pos_responsiveness),
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2),
    active_voter(Prof1,V1), active_voter(Prof2,V2),
    pos_response_pair(C,P),
    votes_identical_after_upwards_move(Prof1,V1,Prof2,V2,C,P),
    num_votes_identical(Prof2,V2,Prof2,N2),
    num_votes_identical(Prof2,V2,Prof1,N1),
    N2 = N1 + 1.
pos_response_check(Prof1,V1,Prof2,V2,C,P) :-
    use_axiom(pos_responsiveness),
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2),
    active_voter(Prof1,V1), active_voter(Prof2,V2),
    pos_response_pair(C,P),
    votes_identical(Prof1,V1,Prof2,V2),
    num_votes_identical(Prof2,V2,Prof2,N2),
    num_votes_identical(Prof2,V2,Prof1,N1),
    N2 = N1 - 1.
pos_response_check(Prof1,V1,Prof2,V2,C,P) :-
    use_axiom(pos_responsiveness),
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2),
    active_voter(Prof1,V1), active_voter(Prof2,V2),
    pos_response_pair(C,P),
    not votes_identical_after_upwards_move(Prof1,V1,Prof2,V2,C,P),
    not votes_identical(Prof1,V1,Prof2,V2),
    num_votes_identical(Prof2,V2,Prof2,N2),
    num_votes_identical(Prof2,V2,Prof1,N1),
    N2 = N1.
axiom_applicable(double(Prof1,Prof2),pos_responsiveness(V,C,P)) :-
    use_axiom(pos_responsiveness),
    pos_axiom_instance(double(Prof1,Prof2),pos_responsiveness(V,C,P)),
    active_profile(Prof1), active_profile(Prof2),
    num_active_voters(Prof1,N), num_active_voters(Prof2,N),
    pos_response_check(Prof1,V,Prof2,V2,C,P) : active_voter(Prof2,V2).

%%% Guess the right amount of axiom instances to use
num_axiom_instances { use_axiom_instance(Profiles,Axiom) :
    axiom_applicable(Profiles,Axiom) } num_axiom_instances.
% use_axiom_instance(Profiles,Axiom) :-
%     axiom_applicable(Profiles,Axiom).

%%% Keep track of which axioms have instances used
is_used(pareto) :- use_axiom_instance(Pr,pareto(C)).
is_used(unanimity) :- use_axiom_instance(Pr,unanimity).
is_used(faithfulness) :- use_axiom_instance(Pr,faithfulness).
is_used(cancellation) :- use_axiom_instance(Pr,cancellation).
is_used(reinforcement) :- use_axiom_instance(Pr,reinforcement).
is_used(condorcet) :- use_axiom_instance(Pr,condorcet(C)).
is_used(neutrality2) :- use_axiom_instance(Pr,neutrality2(C1,C2)).
is_used(pos_responsiveness) :- use_axiom_instance(Pr,pos_responsiveness(V,C,P)).

polarity_axiom_used :- is_used(pareto).
polarity_axiom_used :- is_used(unanimity).
polarity_axiom_used :- is_used(faithfulness).
polarity_axiom_used :- is_used(condorcet).
polarity_axiom_used :- is_used(pos_responsiveness).
:- requires_polarity_axiom, not polarity_axiom_used.

%%% Redundant constraint: only use subsequent profile numbers
:- profile_num(Prof), profile_num(Prof+1),
    profile_used(Prof+1), not profile_used(Prof).

%%% Symmetry breaking: only guess profiles that are actually used
profile_used(Prof) :- use_axiom_instance(single(Prof),_).
profile_used(Prof) :- use_axiom_instance(double(Prof,_),_).
profile_used(Prof) :- use_axiom_instance(double(_,Prof),_).
profile_used(Prof) :- use_axiom_instance(triple(Prof,_,_),_).
profile_used(Prof) :- use_axiom_instance(triple(_,Prof,_),_).
profile_used(Prof) :- use_axiom_instance(triple(_,_,Prof),_).
:- active_profile(Prof), not profile_used(Prof).

%%% Symmetry breaking: only use profiles that are connected to the target
profile_connected(1).
profile_connected(Prof1) :-
    profile_connected(Prof2),
    use_axiom_instance(double(Prof1,Prof2),_).
profile_connected(Prof1) :-
    profile_connected(Prof2),
    use_axiom_instance(double(Prof2,Prof1),_).
profile_connected(Prof1) :-
    profile_connected(Prof2),
    use_axiom_instance(triple(Prof1,Prof2,_),_).
profile_connected(Prof1) :-
    profile_connected(Prof2),
    use_axiom_instance(triple(Prof1,_,Prof2),_).
profile_connected(Prof1) :-
    profile_connected(Prof2),
    use_axiom_instance(triple(_,Prof1,Prof2),_).
profile_connected(Prof1) :-
    profile_connected(Prof2),
    use_axiom_instance(triple(Prof2,Prof1,_),_).
profile_connected(Prof1) :-
    profile_connected(Prof2),
    use_axiom_instance(triple(Prof2,_,Prof1),_).
profile_connected(Prof1) :-
    profile_connected(Prof2),
    use_axiom_instance(triple(_,Prof2,Prof1),_).
:- profile_used(Prof), not profile_connected(Prof).

%%% Symmetry breaking: ensure that profiles (except no 1)
%%% are sorted by size
:- profile_used(Prof1), profile_used(Prof2), Prof1 < Prof2,
    Prof1 != 1, Prof2 != 1,
    num_active_voters(Prof1,N1),
    num_active_voters(Prof2,N2),
    N2 < N1.

%%% Symmetry breaking: ensure that same-size profiles (except no 1)
%%% are lexicographically sorted
interprof_vote_lex_eq_until(Prof1,Prof2,V,0) :-
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2), Prof1 < Prof2, voter(V).
interprof_vote_lex_eq_until(Prof1,Prof2,V,Pos) :-
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2), Prof1 < Prof2, voter(V),
    position(Pos), interprof_vote_lex_eq_until(Prof1,Prof2,V,Pos-1),
    profile(Prof1,V,C,Pos), profile(Prof2,V,C,Pos).
interprof_vote_lex_dom(Prof1,Prof2,V) :-
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2), Prof1 < Prof2, voter(V),
    profile(Prof1,V,C1,Pos), profile(Prof2,V,C2,Pos), C2 < C1,
    interprof_vote_lex_eq_until(Prof1,Prof2,V,Pos-1).
interprof_lex_eq_until(Prof1,Prof2,0) :-
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2), Prof1 < Prof2.
interprof_lex_eq_until(Prof1,Prof2,V) :-
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2), Prof1 < Prof2, voter(V),
    interprof_lex_eq_until(Prof1,Prof2,V-1),
    votes_identical(Prof1,V,Prof2,V).
interprof_lex_dom(Prof1,Prof2) :-
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2), Prof1 < Prof2, voter(V),
    interprof_lex_eq_until(Prof1,Prof2,V-1),
    interprof_vote_lex_dom(Prof1,Prof2,V).
:- profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2), Prof1 < Prof2,
    num_active_voters(Prof1,N), num_active_voters(Prof2,N),
    interprof_lex_dom(Prof2,Prof1).

% Profiles
glue(profile(Prof,V,Cand,Pos)) :-
    profile_num(Prof), voter(V), candidate(Cand), position(Pos).

% Axiom instances used
glue(use_axiom_instance(Profiles,Axiom)) :- pos_axiom_instance(Profiles,Axiom).

%%% Guess (irresolute) outcomes for all profiles
1 { outcome(Prof,C) : candidate(C) } :- profile_num(Prof).

%%% Make sure that the outcome for profile 1 differs from the target outcome
target_outcome_differs :-
    outcome(1,C), not target_outcome(C), candidate(C).
target_outcome_differs :-
    not outcome(1,C), target_outcome(C), candidate(C).
:- not target_outcome_differs.

%%% Heuristic: satisfy as many axioms as possible
#heuristic falsified(pos_axiom_instance(Profiles,Axiom)) :
    use_axiom_instance(Profiles,Axiom). [20,false]
#heuristic falsified(pos_axiom_instance(Profiles,Axiom)) :
    pos_axiom_instance(Profiles,Axiom). [10,false]

%%% Make sure that the outcomes satisfy all used axiom instances
:- use_axiom_instance(Profiles,Axiom),
    falsified(pos_axiom_instance(Profiles,Axiom)).
%%% PARETO
falsified(pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),pareto(C))) :-
    pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),pareto(C)),
    outcome(Prof,C).
%%% FAITHFULNESS
falsified(pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),faithfulness)) :-
    pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),faithfulness),
    profile(Prof,1,C,1), not outcome(Prof,C).
falsified(pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),faithfulness)) :-
    pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),faithfulness),
    profile(Prof,1,C1,1),
    outcome(Prof,C2), candidate(C2), C1 != C2.
%%% UNANIMITY
falsified(pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),unanimity)) :-
    pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),unanimity),
    profile(Prof,1,C,1), not outcome(Prof,C).
falsified(pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),unanimity)) :-
    pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),unanimity),
    profile(Prof,1,C1,1),
    outcome(Prof,C2), candidate(C2), C1 != C2.
%%% CANCELLATION
falsified(pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),cancellation)) :-
    pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),cancellation),
    not outcome(Prof,C), candidate(C).
%%% REINFORCEMENT
outcomes_intersect(Prof1,Prof2) :-
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2), Prof1 <= Prof2,
    outcome(Prof1,C), outcome(Prof2,C), candidate(C).
falsified(pos_axiom_instance(triple(Prof1,Prof2,Prof3),reinforcement)) :-
    pos_axiom_instance(triple(Prof1,Prof2,Prof3),reinforcement),
    outcomes_intersect(Prof1,Prof2),
    outcome(Prof3,C), not outcome(Prof1,C).
falsified(pos_axiom_instance(triple(Prof1,Prof2,Prof3),reinforcement)) :-
    pos_axiom_instance(triple(Prof1,Prof2,Prof3),reinforcement),
    outcomes_intersect(Prof1,Prof2),
    outcome(Prof3,C), not outcome(Prof2,C).
falsified(pos_axiom_instance(triple(Prof1,Prof2,Prof3),reinforcement)) :-
    pos_axiom_instance(triple(Prof1,Prof2,Prof3),reinforcement),
    outcomes_intersect(Prof1,Prof2),
    outcome(Prof1,C), outcome(Prof2,C), not outcome(Prof3,C).
%%% CONDORCET
falsified(pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),condorcet(C))) :-
    pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),condorcet(C)),
    not outcome(Prof,C).
falsified(pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),condorcet(C1))) :-
    pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),condorcet(C1)),
    outcome(Prof,C2), candidate(C2), C1 != C2.
%%% NEUTRALITY/2
falsified(pos_axiom_instance(double(Prof1,Prof2),neutrality2(C1,C2))) :-
    pos_axiom_instance(double(Prof1,Prof2),neutrality2(C1,C2)),
    swap(C1,C2,CS1,CS2), candidate(CS1),
    outcome(Prof1,CS1), not outcome(Prof2,CS2).
falsified(pos_axiom_instance(double(Prof1,Prof2),neutrality2(C1,C2))) :-
    pos_axiom_instance(double(Prof1,Prof2),neutrality2(C1,C2)),
    swap(C1,C2,CS1,CS2), candidate(CS1),
    outcome(Prof2,CS2), not outcome(Prof1,CS1).
%%% POSITIVE RESPONSIVENESS
falsified(pos_axiom_instance(double(Prof1,Prof2),pos_responsiveness(V,C,P))) :-
    pos_axiom_instance(double(Prof1,Prof2),pos_responsiveness(V,C,P)),
    candidate(C),
    outcome(Prof1,C), not outcome(Prof2,C).
falsified(pos_axiom_instance(double(Prof1,Prof2),pos_responsiveness(V,C1,P))) :-
    pos_axiom_instance(double(Prof1,Prof2),pos_responsiveness(V,C1,P)),
    candidate(C1), candidate(C2), C1 != C2,
    outcome(Prof1,C1), outcome(Prof2,C2).

%%% Guess profiles
{ active_voter(Prof,V) } :- profile_num(Prof), voter(V).
:- active_voter(Prof,V), not active_voter(Prof,V-1), voter(V), voter(V-1).
active_profile(Prof) :- profile_num(Prof), active_voter(Prof,1).
:- active_profile(Prof), profile_num(Prof-1), not active_profile(Prof-1).

1 { profile(Prof,V,Cand,Pos) : position(Pos) } 1 :-
    profile_num(Prof), voter(V), active_voter(Prof,V), candidate(Cand).
1 { profile(Prof,V,Cand,Pos) : candidate(Cand) } 1 :-
    profile_num(Prof), voter(V), active_voter(Prof,V), position(Pos).

%%% Symmetry breaking: lexicographical ordering within each profile
lex_eq_until(Prof,V1,V2,0) :-
    profile_num(Prof), voter(V1), voter(V2), V1 < V2.
lex_eq_until(Prof,V1,V2,Pos) :-
    profile_num(Prof), voter(V1), voter(V2), V1 < V2,
    position(Pos), lex_eq_until(Prof,V1,V2,Pos-1),
    profile(Prof,V1,C,Pos), profile(Prof,V2,C,Pos).
lex_dom(Prof,V1,V2) :- profile_num(Prof), voter(V1), voter(V2), V1 < V2,
    profile(Prof,V1,C1,Pos), profile(Prof,V2,C2,Pos), C2 < C1,
    lex_eq_until(Prof,V1,V2,Pos-1).
:- profile_num(Prof), lex_dom(Prof,V1,V2), voter(V1), voter(V2), V1 < V2,
    active_voter(Prof,V1), active_voter(Prof,V2).

%%% Make sure that the target profile appears with index 1
:- not profile(1,V,Cand,Pos), target_profile(V,Cand,Pos).
target_active_voter(V) :- target_profile(V,_,_).
:- active_voter(1,V), not target_active_voter(V).

%%% Shared for applicability of various axioms
num_active_voters(Prof,Num) :-
    profile_num(Prof), Num = #count { V : active_voter(Prof,V) }.
votes_identical(Prof1,V1,Prof2,V2) :-
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2),
    active_voter(Prof1,V1), active_voter(Prof2,V2),
    profile(Prof1,V1,C,P) : profile(Prof2,V2,C,P).
num_votes_identical(Prof1,V1,Prof2,N) :-
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2), voter(V1),
    N = #count { V2 : voter(V2), votes_identical(Prof1,V1,Prof2,V2) }.

%%% Applicability of PARETO
dominates_in_voter(Prof,V,C1,C2) :-
    use_axiom(pareto),
    profile_num(Prof), active_voter(Prof,V),
    candidate(C1), candidate(C2), C1 != C2,
    profile(Prof,V,C1,P1), profile(Prof,V,C2,P2), P1 < P2.
dominates_in_profile(Prof,C1,C2) :-
    use_axiom(pareto),
    profile_num(Prof),
    candidate(C1), candidate(C2), C1 != C2,
    dominates_in_voter(Prof,V,C1,C2) : active_voter(Prof,V).
axiom_applicable(single(Prof),pareto(C2)) :-
    use_axiom(pareto),
    pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),pareto(C2)),
    active_profile(Prof),
    dominates_in_profile(Prof,C1,C2), candidate(C1), C1 != C2.

%%% Applicability of FAITHFULNESS
axiom_applicable(single(Prof),faithfulness) :-
    use_axiom(faithfulness),
    pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),faithfulness),
    active_profile(Prof),
    active_voter(Prof,1), not active_voter(Prof,2).

%%% Applicability of UNANIMITY
axiom_applicable(single(Prof),unanimity) :-
    use_axiom(unanimity),
    pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),unanimity),
    active_profile(Prof), candidate(C),
    profile(Prof,V,C,1) : active_voter(Prof,V).

%%% Applicability of CANCELLATION
num_active_voters_even(Prof) :-
    use_axiom(cancellation),
    num_active_voters(Prof,Num), Num \ 2 == 0.
cancellation_flipped_pair(Prof,V1,V2) :-
    use_axiom(cancellation),
    num_active_voters_even(Prof), num_active_voters(Prof,Num),
    active_voter(Prof,V1), active_voter(Prof,V2), V1 < V2,
    V1 <= Num/2, V2 == Num-V1+1.
cancellation_identical_pair(Prof,V1,V2) :-
    use_axiom(cancellation),
    num_active_voters_even(Prof), num_active_voters(Prof,Num),
    active_voter(Prof,V1), active_voter(Prof,V2), V1 < V2,
    V1 <= Num/2, V2 <= Num/2.
cancellation_identical_pair(Prof,V1,V2) :-
    use_axiom(cancellation),
    num_active_voters_even(Prof), num_active_voters(Prof,Num),
    active_voter(Prof,V1), active_voter(Prof,V2), V1 < V2,
    V1 > Num/2, V2 > Num/2.
votes_identical(Prof,V1,V2) :-
    votes_identical(Prof,V1,Prof,V2), V1 < V2.
votes_flipped(Prof,V1,V2) :-
    use_axiom(cancellation),
    profile_num(Prof), active_voter(Prof,V1), active_voter(Prof,V2), V1 < V2,
    profile(Prof,V2,C,num_candidates-P+1) : profile(Prof,V1,C,P).
axiom_applicable(single(Prof),cancellation) :-
    use_axiom(cancellation),
    pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),cancellation),
    active_profile(Prof),
    num_active_voters_even(Prof),
    votes_identical(Prof,V1,V2) : cancellation_identical_pair(Prof,V1,V2);
    votes_flipped(Prof,V1,V2) : cancellation_flipped_pair(Prof,V1,V2).

%%% Applicability of REINFORCEMENT
reinforcement_count_check(triple(Prof1,Prof2,Prof3),V) :-
    use_axiom(reinforcement),
    pos_axiom_instance(triple(Prof1,Prof2,Prof3),reinforcement),
    active_voter(Prof3,V),
    num_votes_identical(Prof3,V,Prof1,N1),
    num_votes_identical(Prof3,V,Prof2,N2),
    num_votes_identical(Prof3,V,Prof3,N3),
    N3 = N1 + N2.
axiom_applicable(triple(Prof1,Prof2,Prof3),reinforcement) :-
    use_axiom(reinforcement),
    pos_axiom_instance(triple(Prof1,Prof2,Prof3),reinforcement),
    active_profile(Prof1), active_profile(Prof2), active_profile(Prof3),
    num_active_voters(Prof1,N1), num_active_voters(Prof2,N2),
    num_active_voters(Prof3,N3), N3 = N1 + N2,
    reinforcement_count_check(triple(Prof1,Prof2,Prof3),V) :
        active_voter(Prof3,V).

%%% Applicability of CONDORCET
beats(Prof,V,C1,C2) :-
    use_axiom(condorcet),
    profile_num(Prof), active_voter(Prof,V),
    candidate(C1), candidate(C2), C1 != C2,
    profile(Prof,V,C1,P1), profile(Prof,V,C2,P2), P1 < P2.
majority_beats(Prof,C1,C2) :-
    use_axiom(condorcet),
    profile_num(Prof), candidate(C1), candidate(C2), C1 != C2,
    N1 = #count { V : beats(Prof,V,C1,C2) },
    N2 = #count { V : beats(Prof,V,C2,C1) },
    N1 > N2.
axiom_applicable(single(Prof),condorcet(C1)) :-
    use_axiom(condorcet),
    pos_axiom_instance(single(Prof),condorcet(C1)),
    active_profile(Prof),
    majority_beats(Prof,C1,C2) : candidate(C2), C1 != C2.

%%% Applicability of NEUTRALITY/2
votes_identical_under_swap(Prof1,V1,Prof2,V2,C1,C2) :-
    use_axiom(neutrality2),
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2),
    active_voter(Prof1,V1), active_voter(Prof2,V2),
    candidate(C1), candidate(C2), C1 < C2,
    profile(Prof1,V1,CS2,P) : profile(Prof2,V2,CS1,P), swap(C1,C2,CS1,CS2).
num_votes_identical_under_swap(Prof1,V1,Prof2,C1,C2,N) :-
    use_axiom(neutrality2),
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2), voter(V1),
    candidate(C1), candidate(C2), C1 < C2,
    N = #count { V2 : voter(V2),
                      votes_identical_under_swap(Prof1,V1,Prof2,V2,C1,C2) }.
neutrality2_count_check(double(Prof1,Prof2),C1,C2,V) :-
    use_axiom(neutrality2),
    pos_axiom_instance(double(Prof1,Prof2),neutrality2(C1,C2)),
    active_voter(Prof1,V),
    num_votes_identical(Prof1,V,Prof1,N),
    num_votes_identical_under_swap(Prof1,V,Prof2,C1,C2,N).
axiom_applicable(double(Prof1,Prof2),neutrality2(C1,C2)) :-
    use_axiom(neutrality2),
    pos_axiom_instance(double(Prof1,Prof2),neutrality2(C1,C2)),
    active_profile(Prof1), active_profile(Prof2),
    num_active_voters(Prof1,N), num_active_voters(Prof2,N),
    neutrality2_count_check(double(Prof1,Prof2),C1,C2,V) :
        active_voter(Prof1,V).

%%% Applicability of POSITIVE RESPONSIVENESS
votes_identical_after_upwards_move(Prof1,V1,Prof2,V2,C,P) :-
    use_axiom(pos_responsiveness),
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2),
    active_voter(Prof1,V1), active_voter(Prof2,V2),
    pos_response_pair(C,P),
    profile(Prof1,V1,C,P1), profile(Prof2,V2,C,P1-P),
    profile(Prof2,V2,C2,P2) :
        profile(Prof1,V1,C2,P2), P2 > P1;
    profile(Prof2,V2,C2,P2) :
        profile(Prof1,V1,C2,P2), P2 < P1-P;
    profile(Prof2,V2,C2,P2+1) :
        profile(Prof1,V1,C2,P2), P2 < P1, P2 >= P1-P.
pos_response_check(Prof1,V1,Prof2,V2,C,P) :-
    use_axiom(pos_responsiveness),
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2),
    active_voter(Prof1,V1), active_voter(Prof2,V2),
    pos_response_pair(C,P),
    votes_identical_after_upwards_move(Prof1,V1,Prof2,V2,C,P),
    num_votes_identical(Prof2,V2,Prof2,N2),
    num_votes_identical(Prof2,V2,Prof1,N1),
    N2 = N1 + 1.
pos_response_check(Prof1,V1,Prof2,V2,C,P) :-
    use_axiom(pos_responsiveness),
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2),
    active_voter(Prof1,V1), active_voter(Prof2,V2),
    pos_response_pair(C,P),
    votes_identical(Prof1,V1,Prof2,V2),
    num_votes_identical(Prof2,V2,Prof2,N2),
    num_votes_identical(Prof2,V2,Prof1,N1),
    N2 = N1 - 1.
pos_response_check(Prof1,V1,Prof2,V2,C,P) :-
    use_axiom(pos_responsiveness),
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2),
    active_voter(Prof1,V1), active_voter(Prof2,V2),
    pos_response_pair(C,P),
    not votes_identical_after_upwards_move(Prof1,V1,Prof2,V2,C,P),
    not votes_identical(Prof1,V1,Prof2,V2),
    num_votes_identical(Prof2,V2,Prof2,N2),
    num_votes_identical(Prof2,V2,Prof1,N1),
    N2 = N1.
axiom_applicable(double(Prof1,Prof2),pos_responsiveness(V,C,P)) :-
    use_axiom(pos_responsiveness),
    pos_axiom_instance(double(Prof1,Prof2),pos_responsiveness(V,C,P)),
    active_profile(Prof1), active_profile(Prof2),
    num_active_voters(Prof1,N), num_active_voters(Prof2,N),
    pos_response_check(Prof1,V,Prof2,V2,C,P) : active_voter(Prof2,V2).

%%% Guess the right amount of axiom instances to use
% Profiles first (variant profiles-first): every applicable instance counts as used. This is
% a relaxation of the abstraction (no exact number): if a counterexample satisfies all of
% them, it satisfies every subset, and no justification uses these profiles.
use_axiom_instance(Profiles,Axiom) :- axiom_applicable(Profiles,Axiom).
% use_axiom_instance(Profiles,Axiom) :-
%     axiom_applicable(Profiles,Axiom).

%%% Keep track of which axioms have instances used
is_used(pareto) :- use_axiom_instance(Pr,pareto(C)).
is_used(unanimity) :- use_axiom_instance(Pr,unanimity).
is_used(faithfulness) :- use_axiom_instance(Pr,faithfulness).
is_used(cancellation) :- use_axiom_instance(Pr,cancellation).
is_used(reinforcement) :- use_axiom_instance(Pr,reinforcement).
is_used(condorcet) :- use_axiom_instance(Pr,condorcet(C)).
is_used(neutrality2) :- use_axiom_instance(Pr,neutrality2(C1,C2)).
is_used(pos_responsiveness) :- use_axiom_instance(Pr,pos_responsiveness(V,C,P)).

polarity_axiom_used :- is_used(pareto).
polarity_axiom_used :- is_used(unanimity).
polarity_axiom_used :- is_used(faithfulness).
polarity_axiom_used :- is_used(condorcet).
polarity_axiom_used :- is_used(pos_responsiveness).
:- requires_polarity_axiom, not polarity_axiom_used.

%%% Redundant constraint: only use subsequent profile numbers
:- profile_num(Prof), profile_num(Prof+1),
    profile_used(Prof+1), not profile_used(Prof).

%%% Symmetry breaking: only guess profiles that are actually used
profile_used(Prof) :- use_axiom_instance(single(Prof),_).
profile_used(Prof) :- use_axiom_instance(double(Prof,_),_).
profile_used(Prof) :- use_axiom_instance(double(_,Prof),_).
profile_used(Prof) :- use_axiom_instance(triple(Prof,_,_),_).
profile_used(Prof) :- use_axiom_instance(triple(_,Prof,_),_).
profile_used(Prof) :- use_axiom_instance(triple(_,_,Prof),_).
:- active_profile(Prof), not profile_used(Prof).

%%% Symmetry breaking: only use profiles that are connected to the target
profile_connected(1).
profile_connected(Prof1) :-
    profile_connected(Prof2),
    use_axiom_instance(double(Prof1,Prof2),_).
profile_connected(Prof1) :-
    profile_connected(Prof2),
    use_axiom_instance(double(Prof2,Prof1),_).
profile_connected(Prof1) :-
    profile_connected(Prof2),
    use_axiom_instance(triple(Prof1,Prof2,_),_).
profile_connected(Prof1) :-
    profile_connected(Prof2),
    use_axiom_instance(triple(Prof1,_,Prof2),_).
profile_connected(Prof1) :-
    profile_connected(Prof2),
    use_axiom_instance(triple(_,Prof1,Prof2),_).
profile_connected(Prof1) :-
    profile_connected(Prof2),
    use_axiom_instance(triple(Prof2,Prof1,_),_).
profile_connected(Prof1) :-
    profile_connected(Prof2),
    use_axiom_instance(triple(Prof2,_,Prof1),_).
profile_connected(Prof1) :-
    profile_connected(Prof2),
    use_axiom_instance(triple(_,Prof2,Prof1),_).
:- profile_used(Prof), not profile_connected(Prof).

%%% Symmetry breaking: ensure that profiles (except no 1)
%%% are sorted by size
:- profile_used(Prof1), profile_used(Prof2), Prof1 < Prof2,
    Prof1 != 1, Prof2 != 1,
    num_active_voters(Prof1,N1),
    num_active_voters(Prof2,N2),
    N2 < N1.

%%% Symmetry breaking: ensure that same-size profiles (except no 1)
%%% are lexicographically sorted
interprof_vote_lex_eq_until(Prof1,Prof2,V,0) :-
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2), Prof1 < Prof2, voter(V).
interprof_vote_lex_eq_until(Prof1,Prof2,V,Pos) :-
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2), Prof1 < Prof2, voter(V),
    position(Pos), interprof_vote_lex_eq_until(Prof1,Prof2,V,Pos-1),
    profile(Prof1,V,C,Pos), profile(Prof2,V,C,Pos).
interprof_vote_lex_dom(Prof1,Prof2,V) :-
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2), Prof1 < Prof2, voter(V),
    profile(Prof1,V,C1,Pos), profile(Prof2,V,C2,Pos), C2 < C1,
    interprof_vote_lex_eq_until(Prof1,Prof2,V,Pos-1).
interprof_lex_eq_until(Prof1,Prof2,0) :-
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2), Prof1 < Prof2.
interprof_lex_eq_until(Prof1,Prof2,V) :-
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2), Prof1 < Prof2, voter(V),
    interprof_lex_eq_until(Prof1,Prof2,V-1),
    votes_identical(Prof1,V,Prof2,V).
interprof_lex_dom(Prof1,Prof2) :-
    profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2), Prof1 < Prof2, voter(V),
    interprof_lex_eq_until(Prof1,Prof2,V-1),
    interprof_vote_lex_dom(Prof1,Prof2,V).
:- profile_num(Prof1), profile_num(Prof2), Prof1 < Prof2,
    num_active_voters(Prof1,N), num_active_voters(Prof2,N),
    interprof_lex_dom(Prof2,Prof1).

fragments.name: view
fragments.text:
% Each profile is a block of columns: one column per voter, the ballot from top (1st) to bottom.
% Under the ballots: the target outcome (profile 1 only) and, at a step with a counterexample, the
% outcome of every profile in it (a filled letter wins) and the number of axiom instances its
% clause names. Under those: one row per axiom instance of the candidate, with its part in each
% profile it reads: Pareto "¬c" (c loses), faithfulness and unanimity "top", cancellation "all",
% Condorcet "c", neutrality "a↔b" in both profiles, positive responsiveness "a" and "a↑" (the
% profile where a moved up), reinforcement "+" for the two parts and "=" for their union.
#program scene.
draw(layout(grid)).
letter(1,"a"). letter(2,"b"). letter(3,"c"). letter(4,"d"). letter(5,"e"). letter(6,"f").
place(1,"1st"). place(2,"2nd"). place(3,"3rd"). place(4,"4th"). place(5,"5th"). place(6,"6th").
pname(1,"P1"). pname(2,"P2"). pname(3,"P3"). pname(4,"P4"). pname(5,"P5"). pname(6,"P6").
pname(7,"P7"). pname(8,"P8").
notl(1,"¬a"). notl(2,"¬b"). notl(3,"¬c"). notl(4,"¬d"). notl(5,"¬e"). notl(6,"¬f").
upl(1,"a↑"). upl(2,"b↑"). upl(3,"c↑"). upl(4,"d↑"). upl(5,"e↑"). upl(6,"f↑").
swapl(1,2,"a↔b"). swapl(1,3,"a↔c"). swapl(1,4,"a↔d"). swapl(2,3,"b↔c"). swapl(2,4,"b↔d"). swapl(3,4,"c↔d").
swapl(1,5,"a↔e"). swapl(2,5,"b↔e"). swapl(3,5,"c↔e"). swapl(4,5,"d↔e").
width(W) :- W = #max { num_voters; num_candidates }.
start(P,4+(P-1)*(W+1)) :- profile_num(P), width(W).
% rows: 1 profile names, 2.. the ballots, then the target, the outcomes, the clause, the instances
ballot_row(Pos,1+Pos) :- position(Pos).
target_row(num_candidates+3).
outcome_row(num_candidates+4).
clause_row(num_candidates+5).
first_inst_row(num_candidates+7).
inst_row(I,R+I-1) :- first_inst_row(R), I = 1..num_axiom_instances+2.
mid(P,S+(W-1)/2) :- start(P,S), width(W).

% the cells
cellpos(1,M) :- mid(_,M).
cellpos(R,S+V-1) :- ballot_row(_,R), start(_,S), voter(V).
cellpos(R,S+C-1) :- target_row(R), start(1,S), candidate(C).
cellpos(R,S+C-1) :- outcome_row(R), start(_,S), candidate(C).
cellpos(R,2) :- ballot_row(_,R).
cellpos(R,2) :- target_row(R).
cellpos(R,2) :- outcome_row(R).
cellpos(R,2) :- inst_row(_,R).
cellpos(R,2) :- clause_row(R).
cellpos(R,M) :- inst_row(_,R), mid(_,M).
cellpos(R,M) :- clause_row(R), mid(1,M).
draw(cell(R,C)) :- cellpos(R,C).

% fixed labels
draw(attr(cell(1,M), label, N)) :- mid(P,M), pname(P,N).
draw(attr(cell(R,2), label, L)) :- ballot_row(Pos,R), place(Pos,L).
draw(attr(cell(R,2), label, "target")) :- target_row(R).
draw(attr(cell(R,S+C-1), label, L)) :- target_row(R), start(1,S), letter(C,L), candidate(C).
draw(attr(cell(R,S+C-1), fill, target)) :- target_row(R), start(1,S), target_outcome(C).

#program frame.
% the profiles of the candidate
active(P) :- cand(profile(P,_,_,_)).
draw(attr(cell(R,S+V-1), label, L)) :- cand(profile(P,V,C,Pos)), ballot_row(Pos,R), start(P,S), letter(C,L).
draw(emph(cell(R,S+V-1))) :- lit(profile(P,V,C,Pos),_), ballot_row(Pos,R), start(P,S).
boxed(R,S+V-1) :- cand(profile(P,V,_,Pos)), ballot_row(Pos,R), start(P,S).
boxed(R,C) :- target_row(R), cellpos(R,C), C > 2.
draw(ghost(cell(1,M))) :- mid(P,M), not active(P).

% the outcomes of the counterexample
cex_step :- cex(outcome(_,_)).
boxed(R,S+C-1) :- cex_step, outcome_row(R), start(_,S), candidate(C).
draw(attr(cell(R,S+C-1), label, L)) :- cex_step, outcome_row(R), start(_,S), letter(C,L), candidate(C).
draw(attr(cell(R,S+C-1), fill, wins)) :- cex(outcome(P,C)), outcome_row(R), start(P,S).
draw(attr(cell(R,2), label, "outcome")) :- outcome_row(R), cex_step.

% the axiom instances of the candidate, one row each
inst((Pr,A)) :- cand(use_axiom_instance(Pr,A)).
order((Pr,A),N+1) :- inst((Pr,A)), N = #count { X : inst(X), X < (Pr,A) }.
name(pareto(C),"Pareto") :- candidate(C). name(faithfulness,"faithful"). name(unanimity,"unanimity").
name(cancellation,"cancel"). name(reinforcement,"reinforce"). name(condorcet(C),"Condorcet") :- candidate(C).
name(neutrality2(C1,C2),"neutrality") :- candidate(C1), candidate(C2).
name(pos_responsiveness(V,C,P),"pos. resp.") :- voter(V), candidate(C), position(P).
draw(attr(cell(R,2), label, L)) :- order((_,A),N), inst_row(N,R), name(A,L).
% its part in each profile it reads
part(single(P),pareto(C),P,L) :- inst((single(P),pareto(C))), notl(C,L).
part(single(P),faithfulness,P,"top") :- inst((single(P),faithfulness)).
part(single(P),unanimity,P,"top") :- inst((single(P),unanimity)).
part(single(P),cancellation,P,"all") :- inst((single(P),cancellation)).
part(single(P),condorcet(C),P,L) :- inst((single(P),condorcet(C))), letter(C,L).
part(double(P,Q),neutrality2(C1,C2),X,L) :- inst((double(P,Q),neutrality2(C1,C2))),
    X = (P;Q), swapl(C1,C2,L).
part(double(P,Q),pos_responsiveness(V,C,K),P,L) :- inst((double(P,Q),pos_responsiveness(V,C,K))), letter(C,L).
part(double(P,Q),pos_responsiveness(V,C,K),Q,L) :- inst((double(P,Q),pos_responsiveness(V,C,K))), upl(C,L).
part(triple(P,Q,T),reinforcement,X,"+") :- inst((triple(P,Q,T),reinforcement)), X = (P;Q), P != Q.
part(triple(P,P,T),reinforcement,P,"2x") :- inst((triple(P,P,T),reinforcement)).
part(triple(P,Q,T),reinforcement,T,"=") :- inst((triple(P,Q,T),reinforcement)).
draw(attr(cell(R,M), label, L)) :- part(Pr,A,P,L), order((Pr,A),N), inst_row(N,R), mid(P,M).
boxed(R,M) :- part(Pr,A,P,_), order((Pr,A),N), inst_row(N,R), mid(P,M).
draw(emph(cell(R,M))) :- part(Pr,A,P,_), lit(use_axiom_instance(Pr,A),_), order((Pr,A),N), inst_row(N,R), mid(P,M).

% the clause: how many axiom-instance atoms it names
clause_size(N) :- N = #count { Pr,A : lit(use_axiom_instance(Pr,A),_) }, cex_step.
draw(attr(cell(R,2), label, "clause")) :- clause_row(R), cex_step.
draw(attr(cell(R,M), label, N)) :- clause_size(N), clause_row(R), mid(1,M).

% only boxed cells have an outline
draw(attr(cell(R,C), weight, 0)) :- cellpos(R,C), not boxed(R,C).

draw(note("A justification: the profiles (P1 is the target) and the axiom instances that force the target outcome.")) :- kind(solution).
draw(note("Counterexample: outcomes (filled letters win) that satisfy every instance listed but differ from the target in P1.")) :- cex_step.
draw(note("Clause: the number of axiom instances the refinement names; outlined thick: the profile and instance atoms it names.")) :- cex_step.
#show draw/1.
fragments.description: A domain view (Observatory tab): the scene part draws what stays, the frame part one step, as draw/1 marks.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check + relevant   options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check + relevant   options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.add(G.clause(M, X))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))

variants.note: Solve A from scratch after each refinement instead of one ongoing search.

variants.name: record

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction   options "--enum-mode=record"
solver C = shared + check + relevant   options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

variants.note: Keep blocked candidates as nogoods in A (clasp's record enumeration).

variants.name: reference

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check + relevant   options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:

variants.note: Block each refuted candidate on its own: the ground truth on small questions.

variants.name: s6
variants.note: Drop the profile atoms: the clause "use one of the falsified instances" holds for every candidate.

variants.name: fewest

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check + relevant + fewest   options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M), optimal)
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

variants.note: Strategy 6 with the counterexample that falsifies the fewest instances: shorter clauses.

variants.name: multi

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check + relevant   options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        for X in C.models(assume G(M), limit 5):
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

variants.note: Strategy 6 with up to five counterexamples, and clauses, per candidate.

variants.name: partial

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check + relevant   options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on partial P every 8:
        X = C.solve(assume G(P, false))
        if X: reject P with G.clause(X)
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X: reject M with G.clause(M, X)

variants.note: Strategy 6 checked on partial candidates, so one clause can cut a whole subtree.

variants.name: deepen

loop.text:
solver A[i in 1..num_profiles] = shared + abstraction + level
solver C = shared + check + relevant   options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G[i in 1..num_profiles] = A[i] -> C via shared + glue

found = []
i = 1
while i <= A.size:
    for X in found:
        A[i].add(G[i].clause(X))
    search A[i]:
        on candidate M:
            X = C.solve(assume G[i](M))
            if X:
                found.push(X)
                reject M with G[i].clause(M, X)
    i = i + 1

variants.note: One abstraction per number of profiles, fewest profiles first (the paper's breadth-first order).

variants.name: profiles-first

loop.text:
solver P = shared + abstraction_profiles
solver A = shared + abstraction + profiles_given
solver C = shared + check + relevant   options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   GP = P -> C via shared + glue
link   GA = P -> A via shared + glue_profiles
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search P:
    on candidate N:
        X = C.solve(assume GP(N))
        if X:
            reject N with GP.clause(N, X)
        else:
            search A assume GA(N):
                on candidate M:
                    Y = C.solve(assume G(M))
                    if Y:
                        reject M with G.clause(M, Y)
            reject N with GA.block(N)

variants.note: Guess profiles first, test them with every applicable instance, then pick exactly k instances.

readme:
# Explaining a voting outcome by axioms

## Background

A *justification* of an election outcome explains it from normative principles (axioms) such
as Pareto, faithfulness or reinforcement: given a target profile and its outcome, find a small set
of *axiom instances* (an axiom applied to one, two or three concrete profiles) such that every
voting rule that satisfies them must give the target profile that outcome. The idea is from
Boixel and Endriss (AAMAS 2020) and Nardi, Boixel and Endriss (AAMAS 2022); the ASP encoding is
`explain1.lp` of the declarative-cegar repository.

The problem is Σ2P-shaped: *there is* a set of axiom instances (with the profiles they need) such
that *every* outcome assignment that satisfies them gives the target outcome. That is a CEGAR loop.

The loops in this project are starting points for an investigation: which loop suits this
problem, and why?

## The loop

- **Abstraction (A)**: guesses up to `num_profiles` profiles (profile 1 is the target) and exactly
  `num_axiom_instances` applicable axiom instances on them, with symmetry breaking.
- **Check (C)**: looks for outcomes of all profiles that satisfy every chosen axiom instance but
  differ from the target outcome on profile 1. Such outcomes are the counterexample.
- **Refinement**: a clause over the interface atoms that are `relevant/1` for the counterexample.
  The default loop is Shape 1 (`search A`) with refinement strategy 2.

## Fragments

- `shared`, `abstraction`, `glue`, `check`: the encoding of `explain1.lp`, split into the solvers.
- `relevant` (strategy 2) and `relevant_s1`, `relevant_s3`, `relevant_s4`, `relevant_s5`: the five
  refinement strategies of the original file. All five call every profile atom relevant; they
  differ in which axiom-instance atoms they add: 1 the instances the outcomes falsify, 2 those
  they do not falsify, 3 those the candidate does not use, 4 those the candidate uses, 5 all.
- `relevant_s6`: strategy 6, added here. It calls relevant the instances the outcomes falsify,
  and of the profile atoms only the top choice of voter 1 (which faithfulness and unanimity read).
  The idea: whether an outcome assignment falsifies an instance depends on the outcomes of the
  profile numbers, not on what the profiles are, so the clause need not mention the candidate's
  profiles. It reads as "use one of the instances this counterexample falsifies".
- `fewest`: a `#minimize` for the check, the counterexample that falsifies the fewest instances.
- `level`: for `deepen`, member i of the solver family uses exactly i profiles.
- `abstraction_profiles`, `glue_profiles`, `profiles_given`: for `profiles-first`.
- `view`: a domain view for the Observatory tab.

## Variants

| Variant | What changes |
|---|---|
| default | Shape 1 (`search A`), strategy 2 |
| s1, s3, s4, s5 | another of the original strategies |
| record | Shape 1 with `--enum-mode=record` on A: blocked candidates stay as nogoods |
| shape2 | a Shape 2 loop (solve A again after each refinement) |
| reference | the blocking loop (`G.block(M)`) |
| s6 | Shape 1 with strategy 6 |
| fewest | s6 with an optimal check (`#minimize` the falsified instances) |
| multi | s6 with up to 5 counterexamples per candidate (`C.models(..., limit 5)`), one clause each |
| partial | s6 with checks at partial assignments (`on partial P every 8`, open atoms false) |
| deepen | the paper's breadth-first idea: a solver family `A[i]` that uses exactly i profiles, i = 1, 2, ...; the counterexamples of lower levels refine the higher ones before they start |
| profiles-first | two levels (the "two-step procedure" of the original file): P guesses profiles and uses *every* applicable instance; if a counterexample survives that, P is refined; else an inner search of A picks exactly k instances on these profiles |

## Instances

- Questions from `explain1.lp` (tags `original`, `no-solution`). The file's questions with one or
  two candidates (no refinement at all) are left out, and so is its largest one (k = 8, profiles
  of up to 5 voters). `cancel-reinf-posresp-k4` is the question the original file has switched
  on. The default instance is `faith-pareto-neutral-reinf-k4`.
- Seven generated questions, `random-1` … `random-7` (generator `vote-question`: `a` random
  axioms, a sorted random target profile of `v` voters, a random outcome).
- 17 questions from Nardi, Boixel and Endriss (tag `paper`), over the paper's corpus
  (faithfulness, Pareto, cancellation, neutrality, positive responsiveness, reinforcement), with
  profiles of at most as many voters as the target (the paper's weak reinforcement):
  Example 1 (`paper-ex1-k2-p3`), Example 4 (`paper-ex4-*`), the six two-voter profiles of
  Table 1 with their Borda outcomes (`paper-v2-*`), the two profiles of Section 4.2
  (`paper-borda3-*`, `paper-borda4-*`), a Condorcet cycle, a four-voter profile and three profiles
  over four alternatives (`paper-c4-*`). The id gives k (`-k3`) and the number of profiles (`-p4`).
- The encoding asks for *exactly* k instances and has no minimality check, so a solution need not
  be a smallest justification, and padded justifications count.
- Each instance records its expected number of solutions where one is known. Instances marked
  `audit: false` are skipped by the audit and Fuzz; runs use them.

The runs look for all solutions.

## Suites

- `questions`: every question, the default loop (20 s each).
- `strategies`: the file's and the generated questions with a count (except the slow one) ×
  every variant (30 s each).
- `paper`: the 17 paper questions × default, s1, reference, s6, fewest, multi, partial, deepen,
  profiles-first (60 s each).
- `generated`: 12 generated questions (v = 2, 3; a = 2, 3; three seeds) × default, s1, record,
  reference.

Read the instance × variant matrix in the Campaign tab, or run
`node tools/bench.mjs voting-justification --suite paper --out rows.jsonl` and
`node tools/report.mjs rows.jsonl` (add `--metric candidates`).

## Comparing loops

Count candidates (each costs a check), time, and the questions solved within the limit. A variant
that finds a *different* number of justifications than the reference is unsound (or the reference
has not finished): the Campaign tab marks those cells ✗. The audit and the symbolic audit check a
refinement's soundness.

The example `voting-justification-ihs` asks the same questions with implicit hitting sets: the
smallest justifications, without a fixed k.

## Open questions

1. Combine loops: multi with partial checks, or multi with deepen for the first solution.
2. Can a refinement be *lifted* over permutations of the profile numbers (a counterexample
   permuted is a counterexample), so that one counterexample rules out many candidates?
3. Would an encoding that builds profiles from instances (a neutrality instance determines its
   second profile) instead of guessing them first help?
4. The paper's derived axioms and implied instances (Section 3) as variants of the abstraction:
   they change the solution set, so compare first-solution times rather than counts.
5. Explanatoriness: the encoding has no minimality check (exactly k instances). A second check
   (no proper subset suffices) would make larger k meaningful.
6. Which of the original strategies are sound? Strategies 3 and 4 depend on what the candidate
   uses: does the audit (or the symbolic audit) find a question where one of them is unsound?
7. Is strategy 6 the strongest refinement that holds for every candidate? Could a clause leave
   out instances that the outcomes falsify only because others are falsified?
8. Exactly k against at most k: how do the counts and the costs change with "at most k
   instances", and with the smallest size (from `voting-justification-ihs`) as k?
9. Symmetry breaking: how much of A's work does it save, and is each of its constraints still
   sound together with a clause that holds for every candidate?
10. Scaling: where do the loops break down as the candidates, voters and profiles grow, and which
    solver (A or C) gives out first?
11. Explanations a person can read: among the smallest justifications, which is the most
    readable (fewest profiles, fewest kinds of axiom)? Can a loop optimise for that?

generators.text:
% vote-question: a random question for voting-justification. a axioms out of eight, a target
% profile of v voters over three candidates (each voter a uniform ranking; the voters sorted
% lexicographically, as the abstraction expects), and one target outcome.
ax(1,pareto). ax(2,faithfulness). ax(3,unanimity). ax(4,cancellation).
ax(5,reinforcement). ax(6,condorcet). ax(7,neutrality2). ax(8,pos_responsiveness).
use_axiom(A) :- ax(I,A), @subset(a, 8, I, axioms) = 1.
% the six rankings of 1..3 in lexicographic order: rk(K, Position, Candidate)
rk(1,1,1). rk(1,2,2). rk(1,3,3).   rk(2,1,1). rk(2,2,3). rk(2,3,2).
rk(3,1,2). rk(3,2,1). rk(3,3,3).   rk(4,1,2). rk(4,2,3). rk(4,3,1).
rk(5,1,3). rk(5,2,1). rk(5,3,2).   rk(6,1,3). rk(6,2,2). rk(6,3,1).
voter(1..v).
pick(V,@int(1, 6, V, ranking)) :- voter(V).
% voter V's place in the sorted profile: voters with a smaller ranking, then ties by index
place(V,1 + N1 + N2) :- pick(V,K), N1 = #count { W : pick(W,L), L < K }, N2 = #count { W : pick(W,K), W < V }.
target_profile(P,C,Pos) :- place(V,P), pick(V,K), rk(K,Pos,C).
target_outcome(@int(1, 3, outcome)).
requires_polarity_axiom.
#show use_axiom/1. #show target_profile/3. #show target_outcome/1. #show requires_polarity_axiom/0.
